([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] (2017–2021) | highlights = * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East co-Player of the Year]] (2021) * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2021) * [[Haggerty Award]] (2021) }} '''Alexander "Sandro" Mamukelashvili''' ({{lang-ka|ალექსანდრე "სანდრო" მამუკელაშვილი}}; born May 23, 1999) is a Georgian-American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall Pirates]]. He attended basketball powerhouse [[Montverde Academy]] after a stint on youth teams in Italy. As a junior at Seton Hall, Mamukelashvili missed several weeks with a wrist injury but averaged 11.9 [[points per game]]. ==Early life and high school career== Mamukelashvili was born in [[New York City]] and grew up in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] after moving to the country when he was a baby. His grandmother, Ira Gabashvili, was a captain on the [[Soviet Union women's national basketball team]]. Mamukelashvili's older brother David introduced him to basketball at a young age, and Sandro grew up idolizing the Georgian player [[Zaza Pachulia]].{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Seton Hall has a player with a ‘big’ NBA future (and it’s not Myles Powell) |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2019/12/seton-hall-has-a-player-with-a-big-nba-future-and-its-not-myles-powell.html |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=December 4, 2019}} He was in Chicago visiting his aunt, noted pianist [[Eteri Andjaparidze]], when the [[Russo-Georgian War]] broke out in August 2008.{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Gary |title=A world away from war, Sandro Mamukelashvili has found a home at Seton Hall |url=https://theathletic.com/154358/2017/11/14/a-world-away-from-war-sandro-mamukelashvili-has-found-a-home-at-seton-hall/ |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=November 14, 2017}} David currently teaches English at [[Blair Academy]] In New Jersey.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=After training like Rocky, Seton Hall’s ‘Mamu’ is ready to be ‘The Man’ for Pirates |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2020/10/after-training-like-rocky-seton-halls-mamu-is-ready-to-be-the-man-for-pirates.html |accessdate=October 31, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=October 30, 2020}} When he was 14 years old, Mamukelashvili moved to [[Biella]], Italy, to attend high school. He competed on the U17, U18 and U19 teams and helped the teams to finish third place in the national finals. Mamukelashvili said that moving to Italy was difficult but his club and head coach Federico Danna made everything possible for him. In 2016, he moved to the United States to attend basketball powerhouse [[Montverde Academy]], where he played alongside [[New York Knicks]] player [[RJ Barrett]]. While at Montverde, Pachulia became a mentor to the young man and introduced him to several [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] players such as [[Stephen Curry]]. Mamukelashvili scored 11 [[point (basketball)|point]]s in a 72–45 win over [[Greensboro Day School]] to help Montverde reach the finals of the DICK’S Sporting Goods High School Nationals.{{cite news |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=Third-seeded Montverde earns a trip back to DICK'S title game |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/third-seeded-montverde-earns-a-trip-back-to-dicks-title-game |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=March 31, 2017}} In April 2017, Mamukelashvili signed with [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] over offers from [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] among others. He chose the Pirates because his high school coach Kevin Boyle had a good relationship with Seton Hall coach [[Kevin Willard]] and his brother David lives nearby.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Seton Hall freshman adds new dimension, ‘will play significant minutes’ |url=https://nypost.com/2017/10/31/seton-hall-freshman-adds-new-dimension-will-play-significant-minutes/ |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=October 31, 2017}} He is fluent in English, Georgian, Russian, and Italian. ==College career== As a freshman, Mamukelashvili averaged 2.6 points, 1.9 [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s and 0.5 [[block (basketball)|block]]s per game and helped the Pirates reach the second round of the NCAA Tournament. His best game as a freshman came against [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] on February 14, 2018, when he scored 17 points and grabbed seven rebounds. As a sophomore, he averaged 8.9 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Seton Hall basketball: Mamukelashvili 'coming out with an edge' |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2019/09/27/seton-hall-basketball-sandro-mamukelashvili/3772961002/ |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[Asbury Park Press]] |date=September 27, 2019}} On December 19, Mamukelashvili scored a season-high 23 points on 8-of-11 shooting and had eight rebounds in a 90–76 win over [[Sacred Heart Pioneers men's basketball|Sacred Heart]].{{cite news |title=Seton Hall storms past Sacred Heart for fourth straight win |url=https://nypost.com/2018/12/19/seton-hall-storms-past-sacred-heart-for-fourth-straight-win/ |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 19, 2018}} Following his sophomore season, Mamukelashvili worked with Pachulia at his Academy in Tbilisi to expand his game, adding a jump stop and improving his three-point shooting. On November 29, 2019, Mamukelashvili scored 18 points on 7-of-10 shooting and had six rebounds in an 84–76 win over [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] in the Bahamas. During the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] tournament, Mamukelashvili averaged 14 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2.0 [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s per game while making 61 percent of his shots from the field and 60 percent from behind the arc. He fractured his right wrist in a game against Iowa State on December 8 and missed several weeks.{{cite news |title=Seton Hall loses Sandro Mamukelashvili for up to 2 months |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28268980/seton-hall-loses-sandro-mamukelashvili-2-months |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 10, 2019}} On January 29, 2020, he returned to the court, playing five minutes in a 64–57 win over [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]].{{cite news |last1=Fonseca |first1=Brian |title=Why Seton Hall’s Kevin Willard was encouraged by Sandro Mamukelashvili’s short return vs. DePaul |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2020/01/why-seton-halls-kevin-willard-was-encouraged-by-sandro-mamukelashvilis-short-return-vs-depaul.html |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=January 30, 2020}} On February 19, with his father Zurab in attendance for the first time in two years, Mamukelashvili scored 15 points and had six rebounds, hitting the game-winning shot on an inbounds pass with 0.6 seconds remaining in a 74–72 win over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].{{cite news |last1=Kussoy |first1=Howie |title=Sandro Mamukelashvili buzzer-beater gives Seton Hall thrilling win |url=https://nypost.com/2020/02/19/sandro-mamukelashvili-buzzer-beater-gives-seton-hall-thrilling-win/ |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=February 19, 2020}} He had a career-high 26 points on February 29, in an 88–79 win over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite news |title=Powell leads No. 13 Seton Hall past Marquette 88–79 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168421 |accessdate=March 4, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 29, 2020}} Mamukelashvili averaged 11.9 points and 6.0 rebounds per game as a junior. After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an [[Sports agent|agent]], signaling high potential to return to Seton Hall for his senior campaign.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Seton Hall’s Sandro Mamukelashvili to test NBA Draft waters |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2020/03/seton-halls-sandro-mamukelashvili-to-test-nba-draft-waters.html |accessdate=March 21, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=March 20, 2020}} After receiving second round interest, Mamukelashvili announced on August 1 that he was withdrawing from the draft and returning for his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Sandro Mamukelashvili returning to Seton Hall after NBA draft interest |url=https://nypost.com/2020/08/01/sandro-mamukelashvili-returning-to-seton-hall-after-nba-draft-interest/ |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=August 1, 2020}} Coming into his senior season, Mamukelashvili was named to the Preseason First Team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]], and he was expected to help replace the graduated [[Myles Powell]].{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Seton Hall’s emerging star is ready to step up with Myles Powell gone |url=https://nypost.com/2020/10/29/sandro-mamukelashvili-is-ready-to-step-up-for-seton-hall/ |accessdate=October 31, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=October 29, 2020}} On February 16, 2021 Mamukelashvili scored his 1,000 career point in a win against DePaul. At the close of the season, he was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East co-Player of the Year]] and won the [[Haggerty Award]] as the best player in the New York metropolitan area.{{cite news|url=https://shupirates.com/news/2021/4/27/mens-basketball-sandro-mamukelashvili-wins-2021-haggerty-met-player-of-the-year-award.aspx|title=Sandro Mamukelashvili Wins 2021 Haggerty Met Player of the Year Award|publisher=[[Seton Hall Pirates]]|date=April 27, 2021|access-date=April 27, 2021}} ==National team career== In July 2018, Mamukelashvili represented the [[Georgia national basketball team]] at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]] Qualifications and the Georgia U20 team at the FIBA U20 European Championship.{{cite news
